claimBindings.claimTextSummary: Lassaigne's Test (Sodium Fusion Test): Organic compounds are covalently bonded and do not undergo direct ionic reactions
claimBindings.sourceLocator: NCERT/SATHEE Class XI Chemistry::Organic Chemistry - Some Basic Principles and Techniques::12.9 Qualitative Analysis of Organic Compounds

claimBindings.claimTextSummary: Lassaigne's Test (Sodium Fusion Test): Heating the compound with metallic sodium converts covalently bound Nitrogen, Sulphur, and Halogens into ionic sodium salts (NaCN, Na2S, NaX) in the sodium fusion extract (Lassaigne's extract)
claimBindings.sourceLocator: NCERT/SATHEE Class XI Chemistry::Organic Chemistry - Some Basic Principles and Techniques::12.9 Qualitative Analysis of Organic Compounds

claimBindings.claimTextSummary: Detection of Nitrogen, Sulphur, and Halogens: Nitrogen is detected by reacting the extract with ferrous sulphate and ferric ions to yield Prussian blue, Fe4[Fe(CN)6]3
claimBindings.sourceLocator: NCERT/SATHEE Class XI Chemistry::Organic Chemistry - Some Basic Principles and Techniques::12.9 Qualitative Analysis of Organic Compounds

claimBindings.claimTextSummary: Detection of Nitrogen, Sulphur, and Halogens: Sulphur is detected by sodium nitroprusside test giving a purple color, or lead acetate test forming black PbS
claimBindings.sourceLocator: NCERT/SATHEE Class XI Chemistry::Organic Chemistry - Some Basic Principles and Techniques::12.9 Qualitative Analysis of Organic Compounds

claimBindings.claimTextSummary: Detection of Nitrogen, Sulphur, and Halogens: Halogens are detected using silver nitrate solution after boiling with concentrated HNO3 to decompose CN- and S2- ions
claimBindings.sourceLocator: NCERT/SATHEE Class XI Chemistry::Organic Chemistry - Some Basic Principles and Techniques::12.9 Qualitative Analysis of Organic Compounds

claimBindings.claimTextSummary: Detection of Hydroxyl Groups (Alcoholic vs Phenolic): HCl + ZnCl2)

claimBindings.claimTextSummary: Misconception statement: Benzaldehyde gives a positive Fehling's test because it is an aldehyde.
claimBindings.sourceLocator: NCERT Class XII Chemistry Part II::Aldehydes, Ketones and Carboxylic Acids::chemical/differentiation test sections

claimBindings.claimTextSummary: Correction: Fehling's reagent is a weak oxidizing agent and cannot oxidize aromatic aldehydes like benzaldehyde. Only aliphatic aldehydes reduce Fehling's solution.
claimBindings.sourceLocator: NCERT Class XII Chemistry Part II::Aldehydes, Ketones and Carboxylic Acids::chemical/differentiation test sections

claimBindings.claimTextSummary: Misconception statement: Phenols give effervescence with NaHCO3 just like carboxylic acids.
claimBindings.sourceLocator: NCERT Chemistry Laboratory Manual::Unit 8 Tests for Functional Groups in Organic Compounds

claimBindings.claimTextSummary: Correction: Phenols are weaker acids than carbonic acid (H2CO3) and cannot displace CO2 from NaHCO3, except for highly nitrated phenols like picric acid.
claimBindings.sourceLocator: NCERT Chemistry Laboratory Manual::Unit 8 Tests for Functional Groups in Organic Compounds

claimBindings.claimTextSummary: Misconception statement: Concentrated HNO3 is added in the silver nitrate test for halogens just to make the solution acidic.
claimBindings.sourceLocator: NCERT/SATHEE Class XI Chemistry::Organic Chemistry - Some Basic Principles and Techniques::12.9 Qualitative Analysis of Organic Compounds

claimBindings.claimTextSummary: Correction: HNO3 is added specifically to decompose NaCN and Na2S present in the extract, preventing interfering precipitates of AgCN or Ag2S.
claimBindings.sourceLocator: NCERT/SATHEE Class XI Chemistry::Organic Chemistry - Some Basic Principles and Techniques::12.9 Qualitative Analysis of Organic Compounds

claimBindings.claimTextSummary: Worked example problem: An organic compound containing Nitrogen and Sulphur yields a blood-red color upon adding neutral FeCl3 solution to its sodium fusion extract. Explain the reaction and state why Prussian blue was not formed.
claimBindings.sourceLocator: NCERT/SATHEE Class XI Chemistry::Organic Chemistry - Some Basic Principles and Techniques::12.9 Qualitative Analysis of Organic Compounds

claimBindings.claimTextSummary: Step 1: During sodium fusion, if both N and S are present, sodium thiocyanate (NaSCN) is formed instead of separate NaCN and Na2S.
claimBindings.sourceLocator: NCERT/SATHEE Class XI Chemistry::Organic Chemistry - Some Basic Principles and Techniques::12.9 Qualitative Analysis of Organic Compounds

claimBindings.claimTextSummary: Step 2: Reaction: Na + C + N + S -> NaSCN.
claimBindings.sourceLocator: NCERT/SATHEE Class XI Chemistry::Organic Chemistry - Some Basic Principles and Techniques::12.9 Qualitative Analysis of Organic Compounds

claimBindings.claimTextSummary: Step 3: Treatment with FeCl3 solution yields ferric thiocyanate complex, Fe(SCN)3, which gives a characteristic blood-red coloration.
claimBindings.sourceLocator: NCERT/SATHEE Class XI Chemistry::Organic Chemistry - Some Basic Principles and Techniques::12.9 Qualitative Analysis of Organic Compounds

claimBindings.claimTextSummary: Step 4: Prussian blue is not formed because free cyanide ions (CN-) are absent as all cyanide is bound as SCN-.
claimBindings.sourceLocator: NCERT/SATHEE Class XI Chemistry::Organic Chemistry - Some Basic Principles and Techniques::12.9 Qualitative Analysis of Organic Compounds

claimBindings.claimTextSummary: Worked example answer: Blood-red color is due to Fe(SCN)3 formation. Excess sodium was not used, leaving N and S combined as NaSCN instead of forming separate NaCN and Na2S.
claimBindings.sourceLocator: NCERT/SATHEE Class XI Chemistry::Organic Chemistry - Some Basic Principles and Techniques::12.9 Qualitative Analysis of Organic Compounds

claimBindings.claimTextSummary: Worked example problem: How can you chemically distinguish between Aniline and Ethylamine using a laboratory test?
claimBindings.sourceLocator: NCERT Class XII Chemistry Part II::Amines::diazonium/carbylamine/amine test sections

claimBindings.claimTextSummary: Step 1: Perform the Azo Dye Test.
claimBindings.sourceLocator: NCERT Class XII Chemistry Part II::Amines::diazonium/carbylamine/amine test sections

claimBindings.claimTextSummary: Step 2: Dissolve the compound in dil. HCl, cool to 0-5 degrees C, and add cold NaNO2 solution (HNO2 formed in situ).
claimBindings.sourceLocator: NCERT Class XII Chemistry Part II::Amines::diazonium/carbylamine/amine test sections

claimBindings.claimTextSummary: Step 3: Add the resulting solution to a cold alkaline solution of beta-naphthol.
claimBindings.sourceLocator: NCERT Class XII Chemistry Part II::Amines::diazonium/carbylamine/amine test sections

claimBindings.claimTextSummary: Step 4: Aniline (primary aromatic amine) forms a stable diazonium salt which couples with beta-naphthol to give a brilliant orange/red azo dye.
claimBindings.sourceLocator: NCERT Class XII Chemistry Part II::Amines::diazonium/carbylamine/amine test sections

claimBindings.claimTextSummary: Step 5: Ethylamine (primary aliphatic amine) forms an unstable diazonium salt that decomposes immediately with brisk effervescence of N2 gas and no dye is formed.
claimBindings.sourceLocator: NCERT Class XII Chemistry Part II::Amines::diazonium/carbylamine/amine test sections

claimBindings.claimTextSummary: Worked example answer: Aniline gives a positive Azo Dye test (orange/red dye), whereas Ethylamine evolves N2 gas with effervescence.
claimBindings.sourceLocator: NCERT Class XII Chemistry Part II::Amines::diazonium/carbylamine/amine test sections

claimBindings.claimTextSummary: Self-check question: Which of the following compounds will NOT give a positive sodium bicarbonate test? Option A: Formic acid, Option B: Benzoic acid, Option C: Phenol, Option D: Picric acid.
claimBindings.sourceLocator: NCERT Class XII Chemistry Part II::Aldehydes, Ketones and Carboxylic Acids::chemical/differentiation test sections

claimBindings.claimTextSummary: Self-check answer: Option C. Phenol is less acidic than H2CO3 and fails to liberate CO2 from NaHCO3. Picric acid is strongly acidic due to three electron-withdrawing NO2 groups and gives a positive test.
claimBindings.sourceLocator: NCERT Class XII Chemistry Part II::Aldehydes, Ketones and Carboxylic Acids::chemical/differentiation test sections

claimBindings.claimTextSummary: Self-check question: A sodium fusion extract gives a pale yellow precipitate sparingly soluble in ammonium hydroxide when treated with AgNO3 solution. The element present is: Option A: Chlorine, Option B: Bromine, Option C: Iodine, Option D: Nitrogen.
claimBindings.sourceLocator: NCERT/SATHEE Class XI Chemistry::Organic Chemistry - Some Basic Principles and Techniques::12.9 Qualitative Analysis of Organic Compounds

claimBindings.claimTextSummary: Self-check answer: Option B. Silver bromide (AgBr) forms a pale yellow precipitate that is sparingly soluble in NH4OH solution.
claimBindings.sourceLocator: NCERT/SATHEE Class XI Chemistry::Organic Chemistry - Some Basic Principles and Techniques::12.9 Qualitative Analysis of Organic Compounds

claimBindings.claimTextSummary: Self-check question: Lucas reagent reacts fastest with which of the following alcohols at room temperature? Option A: 1-Butanol, Option B: 2-Butanol, Option C: 2-Methylpropan-2-ol, Option D: Ethanol.
claimBindings.sourceLocator: NCERT Chemistry Laboratory Manual::Unit 8 Tests for Functional Groups in Organic Compounds

claimBindings.claimTextSummary: Self-check answer: Option C. Lucas reagent reacts via an SN1 mechanism involving a carbocation intermediate. 2-Methylpropan-2-ol is a tertiary alcohol and forms an immediate turbidity.
claimBindings.sourceLocator: NCERT Chemistry Laboratory Manual::Unit 8 Tests for Functional Groups in Organic Compounds
